item.title: Always Sunny Obsession 8/4/2026
item.description:
Like most people, I eat my meals throughout the day while either watching shows, movies, or even YouTube videos. I’ve read articles and, ironically, watched videos that claim this habit isn’t good for us, but my adolescent mind must not care because it seems to love to be entertained. Sometimes, this habit leads me to continue watching shows and videos far past the actual time spent eating my food. Other times, the habit leads me to keep eating more and more food because I become so fixated on the moving images and the process of dropping food down the ol’ windpipe. A lot of the things I watch do hold merit or some level of educational value, so it’s not all just mindless slop. I tend to watch those when I’m not eating. I’d also like to mention that I don’t waste all my days watching videos and shows; I do things of substance.

Out of every show I’ve ever watched, Seinfeld is my favorite of all-time. From March to May or June, it was the show of choice during my bouts of free time and eating. However, after finishing all nine seasons of Seinfeld, I didn’t know how to mindlessly entertain myself during my abundant free time. I resorted to watching A Different World, a show I had previous experience with since I watched all of season 1 in the fall of ‘25. For context, I had stopped watching the show in the fall because I didn’t like that they took Denise off after season one (I now realize that the show is better without her). The beginning episodes of season two were just kinda slow, and I was still adjusting to no Denise. It was like watching Fresh Prince once OG Aunt Viv left after season 3. Don’t get me wrong, I love A Different World, but it didn’t live up to the high I was coming off of after watching Seinfeld. I got to the latter half of season 3 when I lowkey just couldn’t take it anymore; I mostly can’t stand the writers pushing Dwayne and Whitney like every episode. I finally took it upon myself to find a new show.

I searched on Google for “shows like Seinfeld”. I stumbled across an old Reddit article–for some reason, Reddit has the answers to like every problem–that recommended I watch a show called It’s Always Sunny in Philadelphia. I probably started watching the show in like mid june. As of writing this, I’ve just started season 8, so that’s 8 seasons in a little more than a month. I’ve probably watched at least 1-2 episodes per day. It’s probably my second favorite all-time now, behind Seinfeld. I think both shows resonate with me so well because both their characters are such horrible people. Some episodes are a struggle to watch because the plots are just so inherently evil. I think that draws me back; I love it so much that I can’t help it. I’ve even debated buying a dick towel.

As for the actual show, though, I like all the characters, except for Dee because no one likes Dee. Mac’s probably my favorite. I think he has the best quotes and moments for the most part. Charlie’s an illiterate idiot. I think Frank just enjoys acting stupid and doing stupid stuff. As for Mac and Dee, the show just skips past the fact that they went to UPenn, and they're as idiotic as all the other characters.

In the end, the show has really filled the void that I had after finishing Seinfeld. Though I’m not sure what this says about me as a person. My 2 favorite shows center around selfish, narcissistic people who make everyone else’s lives around them worse. Does that make me a bad person? Is that our human nature or just mine? Maybe those articles that told me to stop watching TV while I eat were right. Then again, I probably wouldn’t have discovered one of my favorite shows if I’d listened.

My Favorite Sitcoms

The rest of this post will serve as a ranking of all my favorite TV shows ever. Some of these shows are interchangeable.

  1. Seinfeld
  2. It’s Always Sunny in Philadelphia
  3. The Boondocks
  4. Southside
  5. The Wire
  6. Regular Show
  7. Smiling Friends
  8. Milo Murphy’s Law
  9. OG Spongebob
  10. Anthony Bourdain: No Reservations
  11. Veggietales

Thank you for reading.

item.title: White Suburbia Retrospective 8/3/2026
item.description:
I went on one of my daily walks a week ago. For background, I’ve been consistently walking in my neighborhood either in the morning or afternoon every day I can since December of freshman year (rain or shine). While walking my usual route, I noticed a new Jeep parked outside one house (I think a girl I go to school with lives there). I could tell it was new because it still had the paper temp license that they give new cars. Not only was this Jeep new, but it also had all its doors removed. Now this wasn’t some new sight to see, since I do live in a little white suburb where this is typical for most Jeep owners. However, this experience really made me question: where do Jeep owners put their doors during the warmer months? Until this moment, I never really thought about it, and how do the doors just magically appear all nice and new in the winter? Do they have, like, a Jeep fairy that delivers and takes their doors periodically throughout the year? I’ve also questioned why Jeep owners put those stupid ass ducks in the windshields, but that’s a question for another time. As an African American who has been subjected to white suburban culture his entire life, I’ve been left with no real outlet to answer these questions.

Once I entered high school, I started to notice that more of my “friends”—or at least people I’d known since middle school – began to pick up golf. Is playing golf a rite of passage for the average white suburban teen? Is dusting off the ol’ clubs and headin’ to the local country club to play a few rounds with Daddy-o the Christian equivalent of a Jewish bar mitzvah? This doesn’t mean to say that I despise golf. I love Happy Gilmore and the good era of Tiger Woods. It's just that my name isn’t Lion Trees and my family happens to lack a country club membership and a set of clubs. At the end of the day, maybe I’m just jealous that no one ever asked my black ass to head out there and play a few holes.

One time while I was on one of my previously mentioned daily walks like a year ago, I was profiled by some white lady who claimed to live in my neighborhood. I was on the home stretch of my route when I encountered her and her two giant pitbulls restrained by chain leashes. As I approached her on the only sidewalk on that road, I had on my now-defunct AirPods (they’ve since gone quiet). As I was about to pass her, she stopped me and asked me my name and if I lived in the neighborhood. The music bumpin’ in my ears prevented me from hearing her the first time, but once she repeated her question, I told her my name and that I did, in fact, live in the neighborhood (probably longer than her dumbass). She then proceeded to look me up and down, probably astonished to see a fully fledged “nigger” in the flesh. Her mind was probably wrapped around the idea that some black folks could cultivate some merit and a nice middle-class life in her suburban utopia. She then began to claim that she’d “never seen me before”. I don’t remember what happened after that, though. We probably just said our goodbyes and went our separate ways. In the moment, I don’t think I thought much of it, and it goes to show my complacency in the environment in which I was brought up.

During the fairer months of the year, the white chillun’ at the bottom of the street tend to come outside and play. Coming outside in white suburbia is pretty much against the law for some reason. I know I spend a lot of time indoors, but you could go your whole life without knowing some kid lives right next door to you. Maybe they haven’t learned that Diddy and R. Kelly were locked up yet. Anyway, sometimes the kids drive around on those miniature cars they make for kids. Though I’m too old now, I've always been secretly jealous since my parents refused to buy me one when I was that age. Whenever I tend to stroll by on my walks and intrude on their fun, I never get a hi or anything. Instead, I get stares and cheek turns. Maybe that’s just the life we live. Hopefully, it’s not just the life I live (which it probably is cause my personality).

The necessity of private vehicular transportation is most present in white suburbia too. You practically need a car to go anywhere. Walking isn’t impossible, but it’s pretty much obsolete if you want to get anywhere in less than an hour. In defiance of this car dependency and lack of public transportation, I used to walk home on occasion and to friends' houses. I guess people get a kick out of asking the less fortunate black teen if they want a ride home, because it happened a lot. Fortunately, I know better than to hop in a random person's car; that’s why I’m still on this earth writing this at my desk. When living in white suburbia, it’s not crazy to see more fortunate people driving around in their little golf carts (on the same road as cars btw). I don’t know anyone personally with one (it tends to be the people that live on or nearer to the lake), but I think these people own these golf carts as a sole alternative to actually driving their other cars. It’s insane. These same people allow their kids, UNDER the age of sixteen, to drive THEIR golf carts on the road to and fro. It’s bloody mad.

Maybe one day I'll figure out where Jeep owners keep their doors. Maybe someone will finally explain the ducks. Maybe somebody will even invite me to play a round of golf. Maybe I’ll even get my own golf cart someday. Until then, I guess white suburbia will keep feeling like a place I know by heart but never quite belong to.

Please take this as some satirical commentary and not some hateful blasphemy. Disregard the grammatical errors here and there.

item.title: The Car Wash of all Car Washes 7/28/2026
item.description:
I washed my car for the first time on Thursday. Wasn’t the greatest decision because it proceeded to rain the following days, and I drove through grass and dirt. However, it was a much-needed routine cleaning.

I first started by vacuuming the inside with our shop vac. I know that it’s usual to do that last, but I don’t really care. Maybe I’m just quirky ( I like that word, and we should use it more). Anyway, I vacuumed out the entire inside, hitting all the little crevices like an anteater in the process. The bloody extension cable, which I used for the shop vac, kept getting stuck under the wheels of my car. This lowkey limited my mobility, but you know I got the job done anyway.

I then wiped the interior. I don’t got much to say for this. Maybe all the time I spent wiping down dirty tables at work prepped me for this moment; probably not, though.

After that, I started on the actual car wash. I rinsed the entire biddy down. I then grabbed my rag thingy and hand-washed the biddy. I followed this up with another rinse. Following that, I started on the rims and tires. My dad used to utilize my brothers' and my small hands for this task when we were younger. I didn’t know it then, but he had us out there posted up like Oliver Twist or some other Victorian-era underpaid factory chillun. When we used to wash his rims when we were younger, my dad would always tell us it was never good enough; then he would proceed to wash them all over again himself or make us do it again. Although my hands ain’t as small as they used to be, my previous experiences helped me get the job done. Once done, I rinsed the wheels and called it a day.

As I write this, I feel like I’m romanticizing the events of a simple car wash. From reading this, I probably come off as if I’ve never lifted a finger in my life or that this was some eye-opening experience. It wasn’t, though. I lowkey just felt the need to document this experience because it was my first time washing a vehicle that I frequent as the sole driver.

Also, I forgot to mention that I wiped the car down with dry towels after I rinsed it.

That’s all. Thank you for reading.

“However mean your life is, meet it and live it”

item.title: World Cup - 7/21/2026
item.description:
This summer, the soccer gods blessed us with yet another World Cup. A World Cup, spanning 39 days, connected fans around the world to grown men kicking a spherical ball for upwards of 90 minutes across 104 games. That same World Cup started with 48 teams, but ended with one champion.

The World Cup concluded on Sunday with a 1-0 win for Spain over the reigning champions, Argentina. Although the game didn’t live up to the 2022 final, it was still a decent game with its very own antics.

I couldn’t really care that Spain won. I wouldn’t call myself a Spain hater. I just don’t care for them. I will, however, put on the record that I hate Lamine Yamal. I don’t actually hate him or have any reason to hate him (hate is a strong word). I just believe that in sports you need your fans and your haters; I’m a hater.

As for Argentina, I couldn’t be happier that they lost. I’d consider myself a Messi hater and an Argentina hater as a whole. I’d like to personally congratulate them on their inability to get any shots in the final. I still wish they lost to Cape Verde.

As usual, the World Cup produced many entertaining games and stories. As an American, I was blessed to watch these games at normal times whenever I so pleased. It would have been nice to go to a game, but I’m not big ballin yet. Maybe in like 2030, assuming the world doesn’t end by then.

This tournament really cemented soccer as my favorite sport. It’s disheartening that we have to go back to watching MLS now and crummy Premier League games. That said, I know that all good things must come to an end at some point.

"Don't cry because it's over. Smile because it happened." - Dr Seuss

item.title: Summer Reading and Sports - 6/30/26
item.description:
This Summer, I’ve made it some sort of mission to read more books. I don’t really have a motive as to why. Maybe it was the allure of embracing some lost inner adolescent self, but I’m not really sure.

Apparently, this reading stuff we used to do for fun is somewhat good for us or something. Despite the allure of that 3hr doomscroll before bed, reading a book and putting down my phone is probably better for me. Instead of looking at someone else's life (which seems quite enjoyable in itself), reading about someone else's life is, for some reason, better for my health. Maybe flipping a page stimulates more hand muscles than the constant up-down thumb movements of a doomscroll.

I find that my mind isn’t as encapsulated as I read books now, compared to when I was younger. I constantly look at the page numbers increasing as I try to hit some sort of page quota for the day. This doesn’t mean that I haven't enjoyed the books I've read so far, but it's not the same enjoyment I experienced when I used to read Percy Jackson or Harry Potter for hours. When I read now, the time doesn’t just float away anymore. It tends to be ever-present, like a constant reminder of how long I’ve been reading and how long I have left to read. Maybe this could stem from a busier life I live now, or a greater difficulty in the books I’m reading. However, I assume it’ll go away the more reading I undertake.

Anyway, I’d like this entry to serve as some sort of log for the books I’ve read since school has been out. The list will expand as I read more throughout the month of July, but this is what I got for now.

Books read through mid May to End of June

  • Wuthering Heights - Emily Brontë
  • Walden - Henry David Thoreau
  • Slaughterhouse-Five - Kurt Vonnegut
  • The Great Gatsby - F. Scott Fitzgerald
  • Murder on the Orient Express - Agatha Christie
  • Currently reading 1984 - George Orwell

I’d say I enjoyed all of these books. However, Wuthering Heights and Walden were very boring at times. Also, Walden was incredibly pretentious and quite hard to read.

When it comes to writing these blog posts, I hope that I don’t come off as corny or pretentious, given that I post on some obscure niche blog in the year of our lord, 2026. By writing these posts or entries, (I ain’t really decided yet), I hope that my writing and grammar improve, so I’m sure I probably got some errors here and there. I think I have been improving, though, because I’ve begun using random buzzwords to make my prose seem more intellectual.

Sports

To end off this entry, I’d like to bring attention to Sports. Regarding the World Cup, I managed to watch most of the group stage games and all of the beginning round of 32 games. This tournament has been great so far. I really hope the final lives up to the 2022 Qatar final. To this day, I truly believe that was one of the best games of soccer my eyes have ever graced

As for this World Cup, I can no longer root for South Africa anymore since they lost to Canada on Sunday. However, I still got the U.S. assuming they win tomorrow against Bosnia. Knowing U.S. soccer, we could easily blow this game, but I trust our team, and CP is back from injury, so I know we got it. The secret to winning is manifesting the victory before it even happens.

The Monday games were all class, especially the Morocco v Dutch and Paraguay v Germany. It was lowkey, just good soccer. It’s always fun to see underdogs beat the European powerhouses. The Netherlands just played bad and their penalties were abysmal. As for Germany, they followed up their disappointing Euros knockout with another round of 32 knockout to a team the U.S. beat 4-1. As for Brazil, I think they’re overrated and probably gonna get knocked out soon. Big ups to Paraguay and Morocco for moving on.

As for my Timberwolves, we'll see if this LaMelo trade ends up working out. Assuming we stay healthy, it will probably help our contention even though we’ll still probably get dominated by OKC and the Spurs in the west for another 3 years. I’d like to thank Naz Ried for his contributions to the team and the city of Minnesota. We’re definitely gonna miss his size and presence now that he’s gone. I'd also like to thank the wolves for deporting Julius Randle to the nets. I’m hopeful for this upcoming season.

That’s all for now.

"For I was rich in sunny hours and sunny days" -Thoreau

item.title: My First Post
item.description:
Welcome to my new website and my first blog post. If you're reading this, you're probably a friend or someone in my circle. I don't really expect or want this to get much traction. that would lowkey suck if i became a celebrity one day and get bashed online some day for some racist homophobic post i made on a blog at 16. Anyway, I made this website because I've always wanted to have one but never committed to it. Seeing as I've had so much time this summer going into junior year, I knew it was the perfect oppurtunity. I'd say it was an oppurtunity well spent. I learned how to code html, css, and some other stuff with a few youtube videos, library books, and some help from Chatgpt. The website is far from perfect rn, but I don't really care. I'd like to believe that watching Dog With A Blog when I was in middle school inspired me to make the site, but it probably didn't. I'll probably continue to make blog post from time to time. However, the more I write this post, the more corny this seems. It also doesn't help that I've felt like the biggest chud over the past few days sitting at my desk making this site. The blog section of this site will most likely serve as like some online diary and commentary for my wacky day to day boyhood escapades. For this first post, I'm sure there's some grammatical errors and formatting issues, but I don't really care for this first post. Finally, I'd like to mention that it probably sucks to read this on mobile. It looks better on a computer.

Well.. I'm done for now, so stop reading this. :)
